To some extent I myself also conform to the above gradient, mostly because of social (and legal) acceptability and limitations to what one can say in public, but to a limited extent also because my expectations (fears and hopes) are not carved in granite. To put it simply: in my younger years I was (to put it simply) a 'one drop' racialist, but now I've grown to the opinion that we're safe if society remains predominantly white. It is not just that I lowered my standards, but also because through the years I observed some cases of people with some alien ancestry (e.g. colonial negro) who did overall look like (and acted, in the good sense) European. I cannot imagine that a genetic witch hunt for these people, would lead to a better society. All in all I even think that in the case of European nations, voluntary segregation leading to voluntary remigration, would be best. That would presuppose an acceptance (not on an ideological but on a practical level) of those non-whites who would, against the trend, chose to stick with us.

But I digress.

Of course, the gradient / cascade of non-whites (from alien-hostile to adapted-friendly) is not the only one. There can also another gradient (an anti-racist / SJW would call it a "slippery slope") be observed: the extent to which people allow themselves to develop a controversial opinion. I've seen several of my old friends move towards 'our' perspective through the years, and none away from it, so that is good.

What I do find worrying that I see more and more people coming out as 'civic nationalists' (they wouldn't use or know that term but I use it here because we understand it) and at the same time stress they are not racists because their daughter is married to a black guy, and/or their children are colored etc. It probably was inevitable that this phenomenon would at one point occur, but as long as the global tide of color is still rising, I'd rather see as little of it as possible.
